title: Sorting: 15 distinct requirements
outcome: Choose order, tie-breaking, mutation and selection semantics deliberately.

steps.title: 1. One dataset, different jobs
steps.text: These 15 tasks reuse the same fictional device shape. Each changes a meaningful requirement: key, direction, tie-break, mutation, grouping or missing values.

steps.title: 2. New list versus in place
steps.text: sorted returns a new list. list.sort modifies a list and returns None. A shallow sorted copy still refers to the original records; do not edit their fields accidentally.

steps.title: 3. Keys and stability
steps.text: A key can be a named function or lambda. Python sorting is stable: equal keys retain encounter order. Explicit secondary keys change that rule.

steps.title: 4. Compound requirements
steps.text: Tuple keys compare left to right. For mixed ascending and descending numeric fields, negating a numeric key can express descending order. Missing values need an explicit policy.

steps.title: 5. Select rather than fully sort
steps.text: When only a few items are needed, heapq.nsmallest is an alternative. Output tests do not prove algorithm choice; the final technique checklist remains explicit.

tasks.title: Ascending latency
contract: Define order(rows). Return a new list sorted by latency_ms ascending. Preserve equal-key order and original rows.
hints: Identify what must change and what must stay unchanged in this task: ascending latency.
The key function should extract latency; sorting whole dictionaries does not define the required order.
Compare the implementation with case 04-duplicates. Trace the supplied inputs and the exact return/output type before changing the code.

tasks.title: Descending latency
contract: Define order(rows). Return a new list sorted by latency_ms descending; preserve equal-key order and inputs.
hints: Identify what must change and what must stay unchanged in this task: descending latency.
Descending changes the sort direction, not the numeric signs in your returned records.
Compare the implementation with case 04-duplicates. Trace the supplied inputs and the exact return/output type before changing the code.

tasks.title: Sort the existing list
contract: Define order(rows). Sort the same list in place by latency_ms ascending and return None.
The caller must observe the reordered original list. Do not replace it with a new list.
hints: Identify what must change and what must stay unchanged in this task: sort the existing list.
The requirement is about object identity as well as ordering; a newly sorted copy is not enough.
Compare the implementation with case 02-empty. Trace the supplied inputs and the exact return/output type before changing the code.
